title: Tunisian entrelac scarf
excerpt: A striking scarf built from interlocking Tunisian blocks in dk yarn. Each square is picked up from the edge of the previous block, creating the classic entrelac grid without seaming.
sourceNotes: Tunisian entrelac adapts the knitted entrelac technique for crochet, working each block in Tunisian simple stitch and picking up stitches along edges.

glossaryTerms.definition: A construction method that creates a diagonal grid of interlocking squares. Each square is worked separately and joined to its neighbours as it is made.
The partial blocks worked at the start and end of entrelac rows to keep the edges straight. Each triangle grows by one stitch per forward pass.
Connecting one block to its neighbour during the working row. In Tunisian entrelac each return pass picks up a stitch from the adjacent block edge.
Starting a new Tunisian block by inserting the hook along the vertical edge of a finished block and drawing up loops instead of chaining a foundation.

crochet.gaugeText: Each entrelac block = 8 x 8 cm worked over 12 sts x 12 rows.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx. 20 cm wide x 160 cm long.

Each block = 8 x 8 cm over 12 sts x 12 rows of Tunisian simple stitch.

Triangle 1: ch 2. Forward pass row 1: pick up 1 loop in 2nd ch (2 loops on hook). Return pass. Row 2: pick up 1 loop in vertical bar then 1 in last bar (3 on hook). Return pass. Continue adding 1 stitch every forward pass until 12 stitches. Fasten off. Work 2 more triangles in the same way side by side.

With colour B, pick up 12 loops along the left edge of triangle 3. On each return pass, pull the final loop through the edge stitch of the adjacent block (join as you go). When 12 rows are complete, fasten off. Pick up the next block from the edge of triangle 2, joining to the side of the finished block. Continue across and alternate colours each block row.

Work block rows until the scarf reaches 160 cm. Finish with a row of closing triangles: decrease 1 stitch at the start of each forward pass by skipping the first vertical bar. Stop when 1 stitch remains. Fasten off.
Weave in all ends with the tapestry needle. Wet block to even out the grid.
